findings.description: Using `or` discards an explicit cause if that exception evaluates to false. Check whether `__cause__` is `None` instead of testing its truthiness.
findings.rationale: If an exception subclass defines `__bool__` to return False (or `__len__` to return zero), raising `TryAgain` from an instance outside an exception handler sets a valid `__cause__` but leaves `__context__` as None. This expression selects None, so exhausted retries still raise TryAgain instead of the underlying exception.
